newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol sets out 1997 spending. [CORRECTED 22:26 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol sets out 1997 spending. [CORRECTED 22:26 GMT]

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol will invest 40.2 billion pesos (corrects from 62 billion pesos) in the Ocensa pipeline project next year and has earmarked 23 billion pesos for further development of one of its fields in eastern Meta province, a company spokesman said Monday.

Ecopetrol chairman Luis Bernardo Florez said that 1997 would see renewed impetus in the company's exploration activities. He said the drilling of five new exploratory wells would begin in the next few weeks.

The final cost of the 500 mile (800km) Ocensa pipeline, which will run from the oil-rich eastern plains to the Covenas oil terminal on the Caribbean coast, is expected to be about $2 billion. It is scheduled for completion by the end of next year.

Ecopetrol has a 25 percent stake and the remainder is in the hands of British Petroleum Co Plc's local subsidiary BP Colombia Pipeline, Total Pipeline-Colombie, Triton Pipeline Colombia and Canadian firms IPL Enterprises and TCPL International.
An Ecopetrol spokesman was unable to say how much Ecopetrol had invested in the pipeline since construction began in 1995.
The pipeline will serve the giant Cupiagua and Cusiana fields, exploited by BP, Triton and Total.

Phase 2 of the development is due to be completed by the end of next year, by which time the fields are forecast to be producing 500,000 barrels a day, BP Exloration (Colombia) Ltd's executive director John Doust said last week.
He said the Ocensa pipeline was as technically challenging as the TransAlaska pipeline, given that it has to pass over 10,000 foot high mountain ranges with gradients as steep as 60 and 70 percent.

In a statement Monday, Ecopetrol said it would spend 23 billion pesos on developing its Apiay-Ariari field. Company chairman Luis Bernardo Florez said an estimate of reserves in the field, discovered in the early 1980s, had been revised from 111 million barrels to 137 million barrels.
The total investment in Apiay-Ariari between 1996 and 1999 has been set at 45.3 billion pesos, Florez said.
He added that the five new exploratory wells would be sunk in the central Magdalena river area and in the eastern plains.
